bull.b: Modest leverage and a substantially larger equity base improve solvency and financial flexibility relative to a more highly indebted structure. This gives Cabaletta greater capacity to continue development activities and absorb operating volatility, although it remains dependent on funding.

The sizeable warrant-related capital infusion strengthens near-term liquidity and extends the resources available for clinical development and operations. Greater cash flexibility can reduce immediate financing pressure and support execution while the company advances its autoimmune therapy pipeline.

A concentrated focus on engineered T cell therapies for B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases gives Cabaletta a defined development strategy around serious conditions and high unmet need. Progress across several related indications could support platform leverage if clinical development succeeds.

bear.b: Without approved products or recurring sales, Cabaletta has no commercial revenue base to fund operations or validate product-market traction. Its financial outlook therefore remains tied to clinical progress, future approvals, and access to external capital rather than established demand.

The long-term expansion of net losses indicates that operating expenses continue to outpace any financial inflows as development programs advance. Persistent losses weaken retained capital and increase the amount of financing or future commercial success required to reach sustainability.

Large negative operating and free cash flow show that reported losses are translating into substantial cash consumption rather than being mainly non-cash accounting effects. Continued burn can shorten funding runway and leave future clinical execution exposed to additional financing needs.
